inputs.source: Published HR policy documents, authored by HR content team, two-person review required before publish

instructions.note: The restriction against giving legal advice ('Do not give legal advice') is enforced only by a single prompt line, with no technical backstop. Consequence is bounded because the agent's only capabilities are read-only policy search and reply, so a violation produces a bad answer, not a security incident.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the credential grant outside the model; the agent cannot read or write anything beyond the policy index regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer outside the model and verified by penetration test; the agent has no reachable outbound destination under any model behavior today.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the chat client, outside the model; closes the common image- or link-based covert exfiltration channel regardless of what the model outputs.

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the HR publishing workflow outside the agent; the model cannot write to the index or bypass the human review step.

controls.name: Model pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The model version cannot change without a reviewed change ticket, so model_upgrade is a governed event here rather than a silent one. This control gates when the trigger fires; it does not stop dependent controls from decaying once an upgrade is approved.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply. A more capable or persistently prompted model may rationalize exceptions or reinterpret the restriction.

controls.name: Conversation / audit logging of each Q&A exchange
controls.decay_rationale: Not described in the artifacts. Without it, the declared A3 'act then report' autonomy has no evidenced reporting mechanism, which weakens post-incident review and attribution.

findings.title: Internal policy content returned to the authenticated requester (intended operation; no exfiltration path found)

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee's own query drives the search.
Reads published internal policy content via a least-privilege, read-only credential.
Source of the quoted content; HR-authored, two-person reviewed before publish.
Reply delivered only to the same authenticated session; no rendering of images or links, no network egress.

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest or MCP config diff adding a networked or egress-capable tool; a firewall or network policy change opening egress for the agent's execution environment.

evidence.observation: Agent credential is read-only and scoped to the policy index; no other tools, no memory, no network egress (denied at the network layer, verified by pen test).
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session; the chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links, closing common covert exfiltration channels.
Only the HR content team can write to the policy index, and publishing requires two-person review, so in.policy_docs is classified internal rather than untrusted.
Agent is scoped to answering questions from the published policy index via policy_search, consistent with the declared capability set.

recommendations.action: Add conversation/audit logging for each Q&A exchange so the declared A3 act-then-report autonomy has an evidenced review mechanism.
When any new tool or MCP server is added, explicitly confirm the network egress denial and chat-client rendering restrictions still apply to it before enabling it.

findings.title: Employee-authored question can attempt to override the behavioral-only restriction against legal advice (ASI01 goal hijack, bounded by narrow capability surface)

attack_path.note: Trusted principal channel, but content can still include adversarial or manipulative phrasing.
Only reachable sink; no execute, spend, or egress capability exists for a hijacked goal to escalate into.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version string changes in config; median turns per conversation rising. Neither trigger adds a reachable capability beyond chat reply, so the tier does not move even though this control decays.

evidence.observation: The only restriction against giving legal advice is a single behavioral instruction with no technical backstop.
The agent's only capabilities are internal policy search and chat reply, so a hijacked goal cannot reach spend, execute, delete, or egress actions.

recommendations.action: If legal-advice avoidance is a compliance requirement, consider an output check that flags legal-advice-like phrasing before a reply is sent.

rating.rationale: Both present findings are low inherent and low residual: the only source classes reaching the agent's capabilities are trusted (the employee's own authenticated question) and internal (two-person reviewed policy content), the only sink is a read of internal data followed by a reply bound to the same authenticated session, and the design has no egress-capable tool, no spend, no execute, and no credential broader than read-only access to the policy index. Network egress is independently denied at the network layer and pen-test verified, which structurally closes the lethal-trifecta pattern (TC1) even if the model is fully compromised by injected content. The forecast rises to moderate only under new_tool, new_mcp_server, or control_removal: those are the triggers under which the network egress denial (ctl.network_egress_deny) could be bypassed or not reinstated for a newly added capability, at which point internal policy content reaching an egress-capable sink would produce a moderate finding. No trigger considered changes the second finding's tier, because its only reachable sink (chat reply) is already at the rubric floor regardless of the behavioral instruction's decay. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.network_egress_deny.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No logging or audit configuration was described; the A3 'act then report' autonomy claim lacks an evidenced reporting mechanism, which is recorded as a missing recommended control (ctl.missing_audit_log).
No MCP, A2A, or other protocol configuration was provided; policy_search.search is treated as a direct tool integration rather than a protocol entry.
SSO authentication strength and session isolation are taken as declared; no identity or session configuration artifact was supplied to verify them independently.
